clue.text: She-devil bringing protest to a head

parts.note: a demo is a protest march or rally
a ness is a headland, a head jutting into the sea, as in Loch Ness's neighbours along the Scottish coast

explanation.surface: A demon in female form turns a demonstration into a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bringing to a head' reads as the idiom for reaching a crisis, but 'head' here is a headland, a sense common in British place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A demoness is a female demon, which is exactly a she-devil.

clue.text: To reveal age of man is out of order

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'To reveal age of man is out of order (4)', gives the definition 'To reveal age of' for DATE but no wordplay for the rest: 'man is out of order' builds no letters of DATE, and no source found gives a fuller clue.
annotationWithheld.clue: To reveal age of man is out of order

clue.text: By nine in the morning set up racing yacht

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: IX is nine in Roman numerals
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: A yacht is rigged and ready by nine o'clock in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns IXAM round to give MAXI; 'By' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a large ocean-going racing yacht, the biggest class in offshore racing.

clue.text: Like a piece by Chopin? Criticise loudly — missing an A natural is wrong

indicators.note: loudly says the word for criticise is to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: to knock something is to criticise it

indicators.note: is wrong says the remaining letters are put in a different order
missing says one letter is dropped from the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written, before an A is removed
the letter A, which is removed

explanation.surface: A pianist plays a Chopin piece badly and is loudly criticised for fluffing a natural A.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loudly' gives NOC, KNOCK as heard; 'missing' takes an A from NATURAL to leave NTURAL, and 'is wrong' rearranges that into TURNAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin wrote nocturnes, night pieces, so a piece by him may be described as nocturnal, belonging to the night.

clue.text: Pleasure as one's invited into weekend party

indicators.note: invited into says one piece is brought inside another, as a guest is brought in

parts.note: Sat, short for Saturday, is a day of the weekend
a faction is a party or group within a larger body
one is I, so one's is I'S, written IS

explanation.surface: Someone finds pleasure in being invited to a weekend party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is only a link; Saturday is the weekend day meant, and the party is a political grouping, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction is the pleasure that comes from having a wish or need fulfilled.

clue.text: Not the sort of horn this hound is likely to hear?

definitions.text: Not the sort of horn this hound is likely to hear?

parts.words: Not the sort of horn this hound is likely to hear?
parts.note: a hunting horn calls hounds, but this dog shares its name with a woodwind instrument, a type of clarinet called a horn, that it would never hear in the field

explanation.walkthrough: The basset horn is an alto clarinet that Mozart wrote for; the basset hound is a short-legged scent dog. The clue plays on the shared name.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset is a short-legged hunting hound, and its name is also borne by the basset horn, a woodwind instrument.

clue.text: A cover is said to help.

indicators.note: is said means the words are to be heard spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a veil is a cover for the face

explanation.surface: A covering is claimed to be of some use.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, 'a veil' is heard the same as the verb for help.
explanation.definitionFit: To avail is to help or be of use, as in 'nothing will avail you'.

clue.text: Sets containing two lots of standard accessories

indicators.note: containing says the first word holds other letters within it
two lots of says the word for standard goes in twice, each copy at a different place in the word Sets

parts.note: par is a standard, as in 'up to par'
par again, the second of the two lots

explanation.surface: Kits that hold a couple of batches of standard extras.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets' looks like the definition, but it is the outer word, opened up in two places.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare parts are extra components kept for replacement, which are accessories to a machine.

clue.text: Passing of politician under terrible strain

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the next piece is placed below, so it comes after
terrible says the word strain is to be mangled into a new order

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A politician cracking under dreadful pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges STRAIN into TRANSI, with TORY placed under it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something transitory is fleeting, merely passing, not lasting.

clue.text: Deadly strength given to team, one from Manchester?

parts.note: taken as written
XI, eleven, is a team in cricket or football
Manchester City is one of the city's football clubs, often called just City

explanation.surface: A football team is given a lethal edge by a Manchester player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given' is only a link. The question mark marks CITY as one example of a Manchester club.
explanation.definitionFit: Toxicity is how poisonous something is, its deadly strength.

clue.text: A celebration mass recalled in Spanish resort

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the whole run of pieces goes backwards

parts.note: a gala is a festive celebration
m is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A festive mass is remembered in a Spanish holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' turns AGALAM round to give the city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a port city and resort on Spain's Costa del Sol.

clue.text: Europeans happy to tour in Alsace? Not half

indicators.note: to tour means to go round, so the word for happy goes round the next piece

parts.note: content means happy, satisfied
taken as written

indicators.note: not half suggests keeping only half the word, here its front three letters

explanation.surface: Contented Europeans going on a trip to Alsace, though not all the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' keeps ALS, the first half of ALSACE. To the British, Continentals are mainland Europeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Continentals is a British word for people from mainland Europe, as opposed to the British Isles.

clue.text: What masseurs might do to socialise?

definitions.meaning: a masseur kneads and massages the upper back and neck
to mix socially with people, especially important ones

explanation.walkthrough: One reading is literal, the other the idiom for mingling with others.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub shoulders with people is the idiom for mixing socially with them.

clue.text: Gymnast may perform this well after applause

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first

parts.note: to give someone a hand is to applaud them
a spring is a well, a source of water

explanation.surface: A gymnast performs well and then gets a round of applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like an adverb praising the gymnast; it is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A handspring is a gymnastic move of flipping over onto the hands and back to the feet.

clue.text: Part of garment with pin stuck in?

definitions.text: Part of garment with pin stuck in?

parts.words: Part of garment with pin stuck in?
parts.note: a pin is slang for a leg, so the part of the garment a leg is stuck into is the tube of material it goes in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin' suggests a dressmaker's pin, but in slang pins are legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A trouser leg is the part of a pair of trousers into which one leg (pin) goes.

clue.text: High priest wrong at heart to pursue reformed alcoholics

indicators.note: to pursue means to follow, so this piece comes after

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, the fellowship of recovering alcoholics

indicators.note: at heart means only the middle letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: A churchman with something amiss in his heart chases after recovering drinkers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed alcoholics' suggests an anagram, but it is the name of the fellowship; 'to pursue' puts the piece from 'wrong' last.
explanation.definitionFit: Aaron, brother of Moses, was the first High Priest of the Israelites in the Bible.

clue.text: NASA tutor turning one out?

indicators.note: turning says the letters of the words are turned into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An instructor at the American space agency produces a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One out' means one out in space; the surface makes 'turning out' a phrase for producing trainees.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels beyond Earth, so is one who is out in space.

clue.text: Unfashionable? Fashionable? Stop hesitating!

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
with it means trendy, up to date

explanation.surface: A string of contradictory remarks about style, ending in an exasperated demand.
explanation.walkthrough: The opposites sit side by side to make a phrase urging someone to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom telling someone to say what they are reluctant to say, to stop hesitating.

clue.text: Jack and one other making big innings

definitions.meaning: in bridge, holding only two cards of a suit, such as the jack and one more
a double century in cricket, two hundred runs, a ton being a hundred

explanation.walkthrough: Bridge players call a two-card suit by this name; in cricket a ton is a century of runs, so a double one is a huge innings.
explanation.definitionFit: A doubleton is a card holding of exactly two in a suit, and read as two words it is a 200-run innings.

clue.text: I'll be seeing you run after Mongol warrior

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first

parts.note: ta-ta is an informal British goodbye
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A farewell, then someone runs from a fierce horseman of the steppes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ta-ta' is a cheery British way of saying goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tatars were Turkic peoples who fought in the Mongol armies of Genghis Khan.

clue.text: On journalists it may urge sound advice

definitions.text: On journalists it may urge sound advice

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them

indicators.note: sound means the word is to be heard spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: counsel means advice

explanation.surface: A watchdog body that presses good advice on the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the body; within it, PRESS and the sound-alike of COUNSEL build the name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Press Council was the British body overseeing newspaper standards, advising journalists on proper conduct.

clue.text: Edible gastropod served up by Italian sous-chef

indicators.note: served up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Italian kitchen assistant serves a dish of escargots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is a link telling where the letters are found; 'served up' in a down clue turns LIANS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Snails are gastropod molluscs, and some are eaten as escargots.

clue.text: Architect's flier

definitions.meaning: Sir Christopher, who designed St Paul's Cathedral in London

explanation.walkthrough: The 's reads as a possessive linking the two, but the architect and the bird are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Wren was the architect of St Paul's Cathedral, and the wren is a small bird.

clue.text: Reptile caught big bird

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A reptile seized a large bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The roc is the enormous bird of legend that carried off elephants.
explanation.definitionFit: Croc is a short informal word for crocodile, a large reptile.

clue.text: A silly, silly expression of agreement

indicators.note: the second silly says the letters of the first two words are jumbled foolishly

explanation.surface: A silly word repeated as a way of saying yes.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word looks like stammering, but the second 'silly' rearranges A SILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic exclamation meaning 'I certainly agree'.

clue.text: Collector at present into gold rings, primarily

indicators.note: into says one piece goes inside another
primarily means the first letter of each of the words is taken

parts.note: taken as written
here means present, as in answering a register

explanation.surface: A collector, at the moment, gets into gold rings above all.
explanation.walkthrough: G and R, the first letters of 'gold' and 'rings', go around ATHERE.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatherer is one who collects things, a collector.

clue.text: Male escort, alone — first to leave after one-night stand

indicators.note: after says the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a gig is a single performance by a band, a one-night stand

indicators.note: first to leave says the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: solo means alone

explanation.surface: A man hired as a companion is left on his own after a brief fling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-night stand' suggests a fling, but it is a single musical engagement; SOLO loses its S to give OLO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to be a woman's escort or lover.

clue.text: Type of drink is old gin mixer

parts.note: taken as written
tonic water is the usual mixer for gin

explanation.surface: A drink is described as an old gin mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: Isotonic drinks are sports drinks that match the body's salt balance.
explanation.definitionFit: An isotonic drink is a type of sports drink with the same salt concentration as body fluids.
